problem_statement: A uniform rectangular block of mass $M = 10.0\text{ kg}$, base width $b = 0.40\text{ m}$, and height $h = 1.00\text{ m}$ stands upright on a rough horizontal floor with static friction coefficient $\mu_s = 0.60$. A horizontal pulling force $F$ is applied at the top edge of the block ($H = 1.00\text{ m}$). Taking $g = 10.0\text{ m/s}^2$: (a) calculate the critical force $F_{\text{topple}}$ at which the block will begin to topple, (b) calculate the critical force $F_{\text{slide}}$ at which the block would begin to slide, and (c) determine whether the block slides first or topples first.
governing_principles: Rotational equilibrium about tipping edge P: sum tau_P = 0
Coulomb law of static friction for sliding threshold: F_slide = mu_s N
solution_strategy: 1. Analyze toppling threshold by taking torque about the leading bottom edge P where normal force concentrates. 2. Calculate F_topple = M g (b / 2) / H. 3. Calculate F_slide = mu_s M g. 4. Compare magnitudes: the smaller force dictates the initial failure mode.

ordered_steps.principle_applied: Torque balance about the front bottom tipping corner P
ordered_steps.equation: \sum \tau_P = 0 \implies F_{\text{topple}} H - M g \left( \frac{b}{2} \right) = 0 \implies F_{\text{topple}} = \frac{M g b}{2 H}

ordered_steps.principle_applied: Coulomb maximum static friction for sliding

final_answer: F_{\text{topple}} = 20.0\text{ N}, \quad F_{\text{slide}} = 60.0\text{ N}; \quad \text{The block topples first at } F = 20.0\text{ N}
sanity_checks: Geometric ratio check: b / (2 H) = 0.20 < mu_s = 0.60 rigorously confirms toppling is the operative failure mode.
Normal force migration: For F < 20 N, normal reaction position is x = F H / (Mg) from center. At F = 20 N, x = 20(1)/(100) = 0.20 m = b/2, precisely reaching the corner.
Dimensional check: Force is in Newtons.
alternate_methods: Torque about center of mass with normal reaction offset x = b/2.
